To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the deuteron transverse-momentum spectrum and elliptic-flow coefficient can be well described in a transport model that includes deuteron production, annihilation, and elastic scattering in hadronization matter, and that the deuteron production in heavy ion collisions is not only a result of coalescence of nucleons from hadronization matter but is also a consequence of hadronic interactions in the hadronization matter.

the deuteron transverse momenta and elliptic flow measured by PHENIX and the STAR Collaboration can be reproduced by a blast wave model combined with a hadronic transport calculation that includes deuteron production, annihilation, and elastic scattering in hadrons.

the deuteron transverse spectrum and elliptic deformation can be well described by the hadronic transport model with the production and annilation of deuterons, and the deuteron transerve spectrum and elliptic anisotropy can be well described using the coalescence of freeze-out nucleon phase space distributions from the transport model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production of deuterons in heavy ion collisions at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC) at Brookhaven National Laboratory.
the study of the production of deuterons in relativistic heavy-ion collisions using the hadronic transport model.
the production of deuterons and antideuterons in heavy-ion collisions.

the deuteron production is well reproduced by the hadronic transport model, which is in agreement with that from the coalescencemodel, while the coalescence parameters obtained from the coale-scence model are not reliable.
the deuteron transverse-momentum spectrum and elliptic-flow data from the PHENIX experiment can be reasonably well described by the coalescence of freeze-out nucleon pairs from the blast wave model.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the coalescence of nucleons from the blast wave model is able to reproduce the deuteron transverse momenta and elliptic flow measured by the PHOBOS and STAR Collaborations, while the transport model calculations with deuteron production and annihilation in hadronic matter are in better agreement with the PHENIX data.
the transport model can reproduce the measured deuteron transverse spectra and elliptic flow at RHIC.

the coalescence of nucleons at the freeze-out phase space is a good starting point for understanding the deuteron production in the relativistic heavy ion collision, but the subsequent hadronic interactions in the transport model play a crucial role to explain the measured deuteron spectra.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the coalescence approach based on the phase space distributions of nucleons produced from hadronizations of the quark gluon plasma in heavy ion collisions is not a good description of deuteron production.

the measured deuteron elliptic flow can only be reproduced if the deuteron production cross sections at low relative momenta are significantly larger than the values obtained in the phase space coalescence model.
the deuteron transverse spectrum and the elliptic flow can be well described by our model, which includes both the production and elastic scattering of deuterons.
